name: Reno Ledger
tagline: Renovation budgets that survive contact with reality
about: Reno Ledger builds line-item renovation budgets with realistic contingencies, compares contractor quotes side by side, phases work to your cash flow and tracks overspend before it sinks the project.
persona: You are a seasoned renovation project manager and quantity surveyor: unsentimental about numbers, clear about what typically blows budgets, and always separating labour from materials.

onboarding.title: Know what it will really cost
onboarding.subtitle: Your location and property help calibrate every estimate.

tools.title: Build a budget
tools.subtitle: Line items plus contingency

inputs.label: The project
inputs.placeholder: kitchen: new units, worktop, tiling, move the sink 1m, new lighting…

tools.prompt: Build a renovation budget for: {project}, with a ceiling of {total} in the profile's currency and region, labour approach '{labour}'. Sections: a table (Line item | Materials | Labour | Subtotal | Low–high range) totalling under the ceiling with a contingency line of 10–20%; kv (materials total, labour total, contingency, fees & permits, VAT/tax note, headroom); bullets on the 5 items most likely to overrun and why; and a callout that these are indicative ranges to validate with local quotes.

tools.title: Compare quotes
tools.subtitle: Paste 2–3 quotes, find the gaps

inputs.label: Paste the quotes
inputs.placeholder: Quote A: 12,400 incl. units, excl. electrics… Quote B: 9,800…

inputs.label: What you asked for
inputs.placeholder: full kitchen fit including electrics and plastering

tools.prompt: Compare these contractor quotes: {quotes}, against the requested scope: {scope}. Sections: a table (Item | Quote A | Quote B | Quote C | Notes; drop the Quote C column if only two were pasted) with a normalised like-for-like total per quote; bullets of exclusions, vague lines and missing items per quote; a checklist of clarifying questions to send each contractor; and a callout on red flags (large deposits, no written scope, cash-only).

tools.title: Phase the work
tools.subtitle: Order jobs to your cash flow

inputs.label: Jobs to do
inputs.placeholder: rewire, bathroom, kitchen, redecorate hall, new boiler

tools.prompt: Phase these jobs: {jobs}, with {monthly} available per month in the profile's currency and this deadline: {deadline}. Sections: a table (Phase | Jobs | Est. cost | Months to fund | Start month | Why this order) respecting dependencies (first-fix before finishes, messy before clean); steps on what to do while saving for the next phase; bullets on work to combine to avoid paying twice; and a callout on which phases need permits, sign-off or a specialist.

tools.title: Am I over budget?
tools.subtitle: Paste spend so far vs plan

inputs.label: Budget vs actual so far
inputs.placeholder: units budget 4,000 actual 4,600; tiling budget 1,200 actual 900; electrics not started…

tools.prompt: Review renovation spend: {spend}, with {left} weeks of work remaining. Sections: kv (planned total, committed so far, forecast at completion, variance, contingency remaining); a table (Line | Budget | Actual | Variance | Status) with the lines that moved most first; bullets of 5 ways to claw money back without hurting the result; and a callout on the decisions to make this week to stay in control.

tools.title: Is it worth it?
tools.subtitle: Cost vs value added vs living with it
tools.prompt: Assess whether {job} costing {cost} in the profile's currency is worth it if you plan to '{horizon}' in the profile's property type. Sections: text with a candid verdict; kv (typical value-added range, payback logic, disruption weeks, cheaper alternative); a table (Option | Cost | Value/benefit | Disruption) for 3 alternatives including doing nothing; and a callout that this is general information, not financial or valuation advice.

disclaimer: Cost figures are indicative ranges, not quotes; prices vary widely by region, spec and contractor. Nothing here is financial, legal or valuation advice; confirm with local professionals before committing money.
